forms: name the number on the card
find the number on a hundred chart
MATH.G2.NUMBER.NUMBER_CONCEPT.IDENTIFY_1.mastery: The child picks out and names any number from 1 to 100 shown on a card, chart, page or calendar, and tells apart numbers with the same digits (16 and 61). Number games with cards or devices are played in class.

forms: match the group to its number
MATH.G2.NUMBER.NUMBER_CONCEPT.REPRESENT_.mastery: The child shows a number up to 100 with real objects grouped in tens and ones (bundles of 10 sticks and loose sticks), counts a collection by making tens, and matches a group of objects to its number.
MATH.G2.NUMBER.NUMBER_CONCEPT.REPRESENT_.hands_on: Collecting and bundling objects from the environment is done in class.

forms: missing number in a forward count
MATH.G2.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.COUNT_FORWA.mastery: Starting from any number, the child counts on in ones to 100, crossing each ten correctly (29, 30, 31; 99, 100), and says the next number after any number below 100.

forms: missing number in a backward count
MATH.G2.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.COUNT_BACK_.mastery: The child counts back in ones from 50, or from any number up to 50, crossing each ten correctly (31, 30, 29), and says the number before a given number.

forms: write the number shown by objects
MATH.G2.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.READ_WRITE_.mastery: The child writes in symbols any number up to 100 that is said or shown, with the digits in the right order and correctly formed (not mirror-written), and reads a written number aloud.

forms: which digit is in the tens place
tens and ones to a number
put the card in the right tin
MATH.G2.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PLACE_VALUE.mastery: For any 2-digit number the child says which digit is in the tens place and which in the ones place, what each is worth (the 7 in 74 is 70), and builds a number from tens and ones (5 tens and 3 ones is 53).

forms: match the word to the number
MATH.G2.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.WORDS_20.mastery: The child reads and writes the number words one to twenty with correct spelling (eight, eleven, twelve, fifteen, twenty) and matches a word to its number.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PATTERNS_10.mastery: The child finds the rule of a pattern counting on or back in ones, twos, fives or tens (35, 40, 45, __), and fills in missing numbers up to 100.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_2D_1D.mastery: The child adds a 1-digit number to a 2-digit number with a sum up to 100 (43 + 5 = 48; 47 + 8 = 55), counting on or in a column, and carries a ten when the ones make ten or more.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_2D_2D.mastery: The child adds two 2-digit numbers with a sum up to 100 (34 + 25 = 59; 38 + 45 = 83), lining up tens and ones and carrying a ten from the ones.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_TENS.mastery: The child adds two multiples of ten (30 + 50 = 80) by adding the tens, and explains it with bundles of ten.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_MISSING_100.mastery: The child finds the missing number in an addition (35 + __ = 100) by counting up in tens and ones, and continues or fills in a pattern made by adding the same number (12, 17, 22, __).

MATH.G2.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_2D_1D.mastery: The child subtracts a 1-digit number from a 2-digit number where the ones digit is big enough (48 - 5 = 43), by counting back or in a column.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_2D_2D.mastery: The child subtracts two 2-digit numbers (68 - 25 = 43; 52 - 27 = 25), opening a ten into ten ones when the top ones digit is smaller, using place value apparatus or a column.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_TENS.mastery: The child subtracts multiples of ten (80 - 30 = 50) by taking tens from tens, and explains it with bundles.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_PATTERNS_.mastery: The child continues or fills in a pattern made by taking away the same number (90, 80, 70, __; 50, 47, 44, __) and finds a missing number in a subtraction sentence (60 - __ = 25).

MATH.G2.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.MULT_REPEA.mastery: The child shows 1, 2 or 3 groups of 2 or 3 with counters and writes the repeated addition (3 + 3 = 6), saying how many groups and how many in each.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.MULT_SIGN.mastery: The child writes a repeated addition as a multiplication sentence (2 + 2 + 2 = 6 is 3 x 2 = 6), with the number of groups and the size of a group, and reads x as 'times' or 'groups of'.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.MULT_BY_1_.mastery: The child gives products of a 1-digit number and 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 (4 x 5 = 20), by skip counting or from a multiplication chart, and solves equal-groups stories (legs, rows, packets).

MATH.G2.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.MULT_BY_10.mastery: The child multiplies a 1-digit number by 10 (7 x 10 = 70) as that many tens, with bundles of ten or ten-shilling coins.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.DIVISION.DIV_SHARING_2.mastery: The child shares up to 20 objects equally between 2 by giving one at a time, says how many each gets, and says the sharing is fair only when both have the same.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.DIVISION.DIV_GROUPING_3.mastery: The child puts up to 25 objects into groups of 3 (or another given size), counts how many groups are made, and tells grouping (how many groups) from sharing (how many in each).

forms: match a picture to a division
MATH.G2.NUMBER.DIVISION.DIV_SIGN.mastery: The child writes a sharing or grouping as a division statement (12 ÷ 3 = 4), with the number shared first, and reads ÷ as 'shared by' or 'divided by'.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.DIVISION.DIV_BY_4_5.mastery: The child divides numbers up to 25 by 4 or 5 where it goes exactly (20 ÷ 4 = 5; 25 ÷ 5 = 5), by grouping objects or counting in fours and fives.

MATH.G2.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.HALF_OF_WHOLE.mastery: The child folds or cuts a circle or rectangle into 2 equal parts, names one part as a half, writes it 1/2, and says two unequal parts are not halves.
MATH.G2.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.HALF_OF_WHOLE.hands_on: Folding paper cut-outs is done in class.

forms: how many quarters make a whole
MATH.G2.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.QUARTER_OF_WHOL.mastery: The child folds a circle or rectangle into 4 equal parts, names one part as a quarter, writes it 1/4, and knows two quarters make a half.
MATH.G2.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.QUARTER_OF_WHOL.hands_on: Folding paper cut-outs is done in class.

forms: which is bigger, a half or a quarter
MATH.G2.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.USE_FRACTIONS.mastery: The child uses halves and quarters in everyday situations: half of a chapati, half of a group of 8 mangoes is 4, a quarter of an orange, and says which is bigger, a half or a quarter of the same thing.

MATH.G2.MEASUR.LENGTH.MEASURE_FIXED_UNIT.mastery: The child measures a length by laying sticks of the same length end to end with no gaps or overlaps, counts them, and says that the same object measured with a longer stick gives a smaller count.
MATH.G2.MEASUR.LENGTH.MEASURE_FIXED_UNIT.hands_on: Measuring with sticks is done in class.

forms: the short way to write metre
more or less than a metre
MATH.G2.MEASUR.LENGTH.KNOW_METRE.mastery: The child knows the metre as the standard unit for length, recognises a metre stick, names everyday things about 1 metre long (a big step, a door's width), and writes m.

forms: read the metre sticks in a picture
MATH.G2.MEASUR.LENGTH.MEASURE_IN_METRES.mastery: The child measures lengths in whole metres with a metre stick (the classroom, the corridor), laying it end to end, and records the result with m.
MATH.G2.MEASUR.LENGTH.MEASURE_IN_METRES.hands_on: Making metre sticks from local materials and measuring is done in class.

forms: how many bottle tops balance it
MATH.G2.MEASUR.MASS.MEASURE_FIXED_MASS.mastery: The child balances an object on a beam balance against items of the same mass (bottle tops, stones of one size), counts them when the beam is level, and says a heavier unit gives a smaller count.
MATH.G2.MEASUR.MASS.MEASURE_FIXED_MASS.hands_on: Improvising a beam balance is done in class.

forms: the short way to write kilogram
MATH.G2.MEASUR.MASS.KNOW_KILOGRAM.mastery: The child knows the kilogram as the standard unit for mass, recognises things sold by the kilogram (sugar, flour, maize), feels about how heavy 1 kg is, and writes kg.

MATH.G2.MEASUR.MASS.MEASURE_IN_KG.mastery: The child balances an object against 1 kg masses until level, counts the kilograms, and records the mass with kg.
MATH.G2.MEASUR.MASS.MEASURE_IN_KG.hands_on: Measuring with a beam balance and 1 kg masses is done in class.

MATH.G2.MEASUR.CAPACITY.MEASURE_FIXED_CA.mastery: The child fills a container using a small container of a fixed size (a cup), counts the full cups, and says containers of different shapes can hold the same, and that a bigger cup gives a smaller count.
MATH.G2.MEASUR.CAPACITY.MEASURE_FIXED_CA.hands_on: Filling containers with water is done in class.

forms: the short way to write litre
MATH.G2.MEASUR.CAPACITY.KNOW_LITRE.mastery: The child knows the litre as the standard unit for capacity, recognises 1-litre bottles and packets (milk, water, oil), names containers that hold more or less than 1 litre, and writes l.

MATH.G2.MEASUR.CAPACITY.MEASURE_IN_LITRE.mastery: The child fills a big container with a 1-litre container (or pours it out into one), counts the full litres, and records the capacity with l; finds how many buckets of a given number of litres fill a drum.
MATH.G2.MEASUR.CAPACITY.MEASURE_IN_LITRE.hands_on: Measuring with 1-litre bottles is done in class.

forms: which month is this occasion in
MATH.G2.MEASUR.TIME.MONTHS_OCCASIONS.mastery: The child names the months of the year in order and links special occasions to their months (Christmas in December, Madaraka Day in June, Jamhuri Day in December, school opening in January), and says which month comes before or after another.

forms: how many days in this month
MATH.G2.MEASUR.TIME.DAYS_IN_MONTHS.mastery: The child says how many days each month has (30 for April, June, September, November; 31 for the others; February 28, or 29 in a leap year), using a rhyme or the knuckle method.

MATH.G2.MEASUR.TIME.READ_CALENDAR.mastery: The child reads a calendar page to say the day of a given date (the 14th is a Thursday) and the date of a given day, and writes a date (Tuesday, 3rd March).

forms: how many claps did it take
morning or midday from a shadow
MATH.G2.MEASUR.TIME.ARBITRARY_TIME.mastery: The child measures how long something takes with an arbitrary unit (claps, counts, drops of water) and relates the time of day to the length of a shadow (long in the morning and evening, short at midday).
MATH.G2.MEASUR.TIME.ARBITRARY_TIME.hands_on: Watching a tree's shadow through the day is done in class.

MATH.G2.MEASUR.TIME.CLOCK_HANDS.mastery: The child points to the long minute hand and the short hour hand on an analogue clock, and says which hand moves faster.

MATH.G2.MEASUR.TIME.READ_HOUR.mastery: The child reads an analogue clock showing an o'clock time (the minute hand on 12, the hour hand on 4 is 4 o'clock) and matches clocks to o'clock times.

MATH.G2.MEASUR.TIME.WRITE_HOUR.mastery: The child writes the o'clock time shown on an analogue clock (3 o'clock) and on a digital clock (3:00), and draws the hands for a given o'clock time.

MATH.G2.MEASUR.MONEY.IDENTIFY_MONEY_100.mastery: The child names the Kenyan coins (sh. 1, 5, 10, 20) and notes (sh. 50, 100) by value, sorts them, and tells which is worth more by the number, not the size or the count.

forms: how much money in ten-shilling coins
MATH.G2.MEASUR.MONEY.COUNT_10_20_COINS.mastery: The child counts a set of sh. 10 coins in tens and a set of sh. 20 coins in twenties, up to sh. 100, and writes the total with sh.

forms: how many fifties make a hundred
MATH.G2.MEASUR.MONEY.COUNT_50_100_NOTES.mastery: The child counts sh. 50 notes in fifties and sh. 100 notes in hundreds and says the total (two sh. 50 notes are sh. 100).

MATH.G2.MEASUR.MONEY.ADD_MONEY_100.mastery: The child adds two amounts or two coins and notes (sh. 50 + sh. 20 = sh. 70; sh. 35 + sh. 40 = sh. 75), with a sum up to sh. 100, and writes sh.

forms: can you buy these with this money
MATH.G2.MEASUR.MONEY.BUY_NO_BALANCE.mastery: The child picks coins and notes that pay exactly for up to 3 items (total up to sh. 100) in a model shop, finds the total cost, and checks no change is needed.
MATH.G2.MEASUR.MONEY.BUY_NO_BALANCE.hands_on: Role play in the classroom model shop is done in class.

forms: is the edge straight or curved
MATH.G2.GEOMET.LINES.STRAIGHT_LINES.mastery: The child picks out straight lines in pictures and objects (the edge of a ruler, a door), models them with sticks or a stretched string, and draws them with a ruler, held upright, flat or slanting.
MATH.G2.GEOMET.LINES.STRAIGHT_LINES.hands_on: Modelling lines with sticks, string and clay is done in class.

forms: is the edge straight or curved
MATH.G2.GEOMET.LINES.CURVED_LINES.mastery: The child picks out curved lines in pictures and objects (the edge of a plate, a rainbow), models them with string or clay, and draws them freehand.
MATH.G2.GEOMET.LINES.CURVED_LINES.hands_on: Modelling curved lines with string and clay is done in class.

forms: name the shape of the object
MATH.G2.GEOMET.SHAPES.NAME_SHAPES_ENV.mastery: The child names triangles, squares, rectangles, circles and ovals in objects and pictures (a window, a clock, an egg), in any position, and says the kind of lines each has (straight or curved).

MATH.G2.GEOMET.SHAPES.DRAW_SHAPES.mastery: The child draws a triangle, a square, a circle and an oval, freehand and with a ruler or round objects, with the right number of sides.
MATH.G2.GEOMET.SHAPES.DRAW_SHAPES.hands_on: Drawing shapes on manila paper is done in class.

MATH.G2.GEOMET.SHAPES.SHAPE_PATTERNS.mastery: The child finds the part of a shape pattern that repeats (circle, triangle, triangle), says or draws what comes next, and makes a pattern of their own.
